part.text: I’m treating “night” as 7 p.m.–6:59 a.m. and comparing it with the equal-length 7 a.m.–6:59 p.m. period. The file can show crash counts and outcomes per reported crash, but it has no traffic-volume or travel-exposure data to establish whether an individual trip is riskier at night.

input.patchText:
*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: out/generate_analysis.py
+import json
+import os
+
+import duckdb
+import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
+import pandas as pd
+
+
+DATA = "data/crashes.parquet"
+OUT = "out"
+os.makedirs(OUT, exist_ok=True)
+
+con = duckdb.connect()
+query = """
+WITH classified AS (
+    SELECT
+        CASE WHEN hour(crash_time) >= 19 OR hour(crash_time) < 7
+             THEN 'Night (7pm–6:59am)' ELSE 'Day (7am–6:59pm)' END AS period,
+        coalesce(number_of_persons_injured, 0) AS injured,
+        coalesce(number_of_persons_killed, 0) AS killed
+    FROM read_parquet(?)
+)
+SELECT period,
+       count(*) AS crashes,
+       count(*) FILTER (WHERE injured > 0 OR killed > 0) AS injury_or_fatal_crashes,
+       sum(injured) AS persons_injured,
+       sum(killed) AS persons_killed
+FROM classified
+GROUP BY period
+"""
+data = con.execute(query, [DATA]).fetchdf()
+order = ["Day (7am–6:59pm)", "Night (7pm–6:59am)"]
+data["period"] = pd.Categorical(data["period"], categories=order, ordered=True)
+data = data.sort_values("period").reset_index(drop=True)
+data["injury_or_fatal_crash_pct"] = 100 * data["injury_or_fatal_crashes"] / data["crashes"]
+data["casualties"] = data["persons_injured"] + data["persons_killed"]
+data["casualties_per_crash"] = data["casualties"] / data["crashes"]
+
+plt.rcParams.update({"font.family": "DejaVu Sans", "axes.titleweight": "bold"})
+colors = ["#4C78A8", "#E45756"]
+
+
+def save_bar(option_id, values, column, title, ylabel, fmt, csv_columns):
+    values[csv_columns].to_csv(f"{OUT}/values_{option_id}.csv", index=False)
+    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8.2, 5.0))
+    bars = ax.bar(values["period"].astype(str), values[column], color=colors, width=0.58)
+    ax.set_title(title, loc="left", fontsize=15, pad=14)
+    ax.set_ylabel(ylabel)
+    ax.spines[["top", "right"]].set_visible(False)
+    ax.grid(axis="y", color="#D9DEE5", linewidth=0.8)
+    ax.set_axisbelow(True)
+    ax.tick_params(axis="x", labelsize=10)
+    ax.bar_label(bars, labels=[fmt.format(x) for x in values[column]], padding=4, fontsize=11)
+    ax.margins(y=0.14)
+    fig.text(0.01, 0.01, "NYC police-reported crashes; time of day only. No adjustment for traffic volume or travel exposure.", fontsize=8, color="#555555")
+    fig.tight_layout(rect=(0, 0.05, 1, 1))
+    fig.savefig(f"{OUT}/option_{option_id}.png", dpi=180, bbox_inches="tight")
+    plt.close(fig)
+
+
+save_bar(
+    1, data, "crashes",
+    "Police-reported crashes by time of day",
+    "Crash count", "{:,.0f}",
+    ["period", "crashes"],
+)
+save_bar(
+    2, data, "injury_or_fatal_crash_pct",
+    "Share of crashes with an injury or fatality",
+    "Crashes with ≥1 person injured or killed (%)", "{:.1f}%",
+    ["period", "crashes", "injury_or_fatal_crashes", "injury_or_fatal_crash_pct"],
+)
+save_bar(
+    3, data, "casualties_per_crash",
+    "People injured or killed per reported crash",
+    "Injured + killed people per crash", "{:.3f}",
+    ["period", "crashes", "persons_injured", "persons_killed", "casualties", "casualties_per_crash"],
+)
+
+print(data.to_string(index=False))
*** End Patch

+    {
+      "id": 2,
+      "metric": "Share of crashes involving at least one person injured or killed",
+      "denominator": "All police-reported crashes in the corresponding period",
+      "grouping": "Day (7am–6:59pm) versus night (7pm–6:59am)",
+      "chart_type": "Two-category bar chart of percentages",
+      "reason": "The proportion of crashes with reported harm compares outcomes conditional on a crash and is less confounded by the difference in crash totals.",
+      "probability": 0.45,
+      "answer": "An injury-or-fatality crash made up 28.3% of nighttime crashes versus 23.1% of daytime crashes, a 5.2-percentage-point difference, though this does not measure risk per trip.",

The per-crash denominator is a defensible severity comparison, but the data lack traffic or travel exposure, so the chart cannot establish whether a road user's chance of crashing or being harmed per trip is higher at night."
+    },
+    {
+      "id": 3,
+      "metric": "Number of people injured plus killed per police-reported crash",
+      "denominator": "All police-reported crashes in the corresponding period",
+      "grouping": "Day (7am–6:59pm) versus night (7pm–6:59am)",
+      "chart_type": "Two-category bar chart of casualties per crash",

+      "answer": "Nighttime crashes averaged 0.398 people injured or killed per crash versus 0.305 in daytime, about 30% more, but that is severity per crash rather than danger per trip.",
+      "interpretation": "This framing answers how many people are injured or killed on average in a reported crash: nighttime crashes averaged 0.398 casualties, compared with 0.305 in daytime. Counting all reported casualties makes it a defensible measure of crash severity, but without traffic or travel exposure it leaves the likelihood of harm for an individual road user unanswered."
+    }
+  ]
+}
